brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: There are two bases: a full hex base (piece:0,0,0;full) and a north-half base (piece:1,0,0;half-n), held together by jointBolt:0#0,0#0. Covers close both tops and 7 caps finish the open edges.

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 is a full bin split into 3 sections. bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half-n-half-div2 is a half-height bin split into 2. Both are separate catalog bins sitting in bin sockets. Lifting them out is my reading of what bins are for; the configurator doesn't test it.
drawer:0#1,0#cut is a classic drawer on the cut face of the half base. The configurator offered it as the only drawer socket and it went on without a refusal.
handle:0,0,0;top sits on the top cover of the full base, cover:0,0,0;full;top, with its 3 inserts. This checks fit only, not how much weight it can carry.

finish.summary: The configurator accepted the build with no rule issues, and its mesh-collision check reads "clear". It uses 19 parts.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
